name: .NET
description: Cross-platform developer platform from Microsoft used to build web, desktop, mobile, cloud, and IoT applications across multiple programming languages.

name: .NET Core
description: Cross-platform, open-source implementation of .NET that ran on Windows, Linux, and macOS before being unified into the modern .NET platform.

name: .NET Framework
description: Original Windows-only implementation of .NET, providing a runtime and class libraries for building desktop and web applications on Windows.

name: .NET Standard
description: Specification defining a common set of APIs that different .NET implementations must support, enabling code and libraries to be shared across them.

name: Akka
description: Toolkit for building concurrent, distributed, and fault-tolerant applications on the JVM using the actor model for message-driven processing.

name: AmCharts
description: JavaScript charting and data visualization library used to create interactive charts, graphs, and maps for web applications.

name: Android Studio
description: Official integrated development environment for building Android applications, providing code editing, debugging, emulation, and build tools based on IntelliJ IDEA.

name: Angular
description: TypeScript-based web application framework maintained by Google for building single-page applications with a component-based architecture.

name: AngularJS
description: Original JavaScript-based front-end framework from Google for building dynamic single-page web applications, predecessor to the rewritten Angular framework.

name: Apache CXF
description: Open-source Java framework for building and consuming web services, supporting both SOAP-based and RESTful service styles.

name: Apache Tomcat
description: Open-source Java servlet container that implements core Java EE web specifications, used to deploy and run Java web applications.

name: ASP.NET
description: Web application framework from Microsoft for building dynamic websites, services, and APIs on the .NET platform.

name: ASP.NET Core
description: Cross-platform, open-source web framework from Microsoft, succeeding ASP.NET, used to build web apps, APIs, and microservices on modern .NET.

name: ASP.NET Web Forms
description: Component of the original ASP.NET framework for building web applications using event-driven, server-side UI controls similar to desktop application development.

name: Aurelia
description: JavaScript front-end framework for building single-page applications and web components with an emphasis on standards-based, convention-driven development.

name: AutoMapper
description: Library for .NET that automates the mapping of properties between objects, commonly used to convert between domain models and data transfer objects.

name: AVPlayer
description: Apple framework class used to play and control audio and video media within iOS, macOS, and other Apple platform applications.

name: Axios
description: Promise-based HTTP client for JavaScript used in browsers and Node.js to make requests to APIs and handle responses.

name: Babel
description: JavaScript compiler that converts modern ECMAScript syntax into backward-compatible versions so code runs on older browsers and environments.

name: Blazor
description: Web framework from Microsoft that lets developers build interactive web UIs using C# and .NET instead of JavaScript, running on the server or in the browser via WebAssembly.

name: Bootstrap
description: Front-end CSS framework that provides pre-built components and a responsive grid system for quickly designing web page layouts.

name: Castle Windsor
description: Inversion of control container for .NET applications, used to manage object creation and dependency injection.

name: CocoaPods
description: Dependency manager for Swift and Objective-C projects that automates downloading, integrating, and managing third-party libraries in Xcode projects.

name: Cocos2d
description: Open-source framework for building 2D games and graphical applications, offering tools for rendering, physics, and animation across mobile and desktop platforms.

name: Combine
description: Apple framework for handling asynchronous and event-driven code using a declarative publisher/subscriber model, commonly paired with SwiftUI apps.

name: D3.js
description: JavaScript library for producing dynamic, interactive data visualizations in web browsers by binding data to DOM elements and SVG.

name: Dapper
description: Lightweight object-relational mapper for .NET that extends ADO.NET to map SQL query results to objects with minimal overhead.

name: Django
description: High-level Python web framework that follows the model-view-template pattern, designed for rapid development of secure, maintainable websites.

name: Docusaurus
description: Static site generator built with React designed for creating documentation websites, with support for versioning and Markdown content.

name: Drupal
description: Open-source content management system written in PHP, used to build, manage, and publish content-driven websites and web applications.

name: Eclipse Jetty
description: Lightweight, embeddable Java HTTP server and servlet container, often used to power web applications and services within larger Java programs.

name: EJS
description: Templating engine for JavaScript that generates HTML markup by embedding plain JavaScript code, commonly used with Node.js web applications.

name: Electron
description: Framework for building cross-platform desktop applications using web technologies like JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, combining Chromium and Node.js.

name: Entity Framework
description: Object-relational mapping framework for .NET that lets developers interact with databases using .NET objects instead of writing raw SQL.

name: Express
description: Minimalist web application framework for Node.js that provides routing, middleware, and HTTP utilities for building web servers and APIs.

name: Express.js
description: Minimalist web application framework for Node.js that provides routing, middleware, and HTTP utilities for building web servers and APIs.

name: Flask
description: Lightweight Python web framework that offers routing and templating basics while leaving other components like databases up to the developer.

name: Flutter
description: Open-source UI toolkit from Google for building natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single Dart codebase.

name: GraphQL
description: Query language and runtime for APIs that lets clients request exactly the data fields they need from a server in a single call.

name: gRPC
description: Open-source remote procedure call framework that uses protocol buffers for efficient, strongly-typed communication between services, often across languages.

name: Ionic
description: Open-source framework for building cross-platform mobile and desktop apps using standard web technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, wrapped in native containers.

name: iOS
description: Apple's mobile operating system that powers iPhone devices, providing the platform and APIs on which mobile apps run.

name: JBoss (WildFly)
description: Java EE / Jakarta EE application server used to deploy and run enterprise Java applications, handling services like transactions, security, and messaging.

name: jQuery
description: JavaScript library that simplifies DOM manipulation, event handling, and AJAX requests, historically widely used to write cross-browser compatible scripts.

name: JSON Server
description: Command-line tool that spins up a full fake REST API from a JSON file, useful for prototyping frontends without a real backend.

name: Kendo UI
description: Commercial UI component library providing widgets and controls for building web applications, with versions for various JavaScript frameworks.

name: Knockout.js
description: JavaScript library that implements the Model-View-ViewModel pattern, enabling automatic UI updates through observable data binding.

name: Laravel
description: PHP web application framework that provides tools for routing, ORM, templating, and authentication to build web applications following the MVC pattern.

name: LINQ
description: Language-integrated query feature in .NET that lets developers write set-based queries over collections, databases, and XML directly in C# or VB.NET syntax.

name: MediatR
description: .NET library implementing the mediator pattern, used to decouple in-process request/response handling and event notifications between components.

name: Microsoft Graph API
description: Unified REST API and SDK that lets applications access data and services across Microsoft 365, such as Outlook, Teams, and Azure Active Directory.

name: Moment.js
description: JavaScript library for parsing, validating, manipulating, and formatting dates and times. Widely used in older web projects, though now in maintenance mode with lighter alternatives recommended for new code.

name: Moshi
description: JSON serialization library for Java and Kotlin (commonly used on Android) that converts objects to and from JSON with reflection or generated adapters.

name: NestJS
description: TypeScript-based Node.js framework for building scalable server-side applications, providing a modular architecture inspired by Angular along with dependency injection.

name: Next.js
description: React framework that adds server-side rendering, static site generation, routing, and API routes on top of React. Used to build production-ready web applications with improved performance and SEO.

name: NgRx
description: State management library for Angular applications based on reactive programming and the Redux pattern, using RxJS observables to manage application state and side effects in a predictable way.

name: NHibernate
description: Object-relational mapping framework for .NET that maps classes to relational database tables, handling data persistence and querying.

name: Node.js
description: JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that enables running JavaScript outside the browser, commonly used to build servers and command-line tools.

name: PrimeNG
description: UI component library for Angular providing a large collection of ready-made widgets like tables, charts, and forms to speed up building application interfaces.

name: Quarkus
description: Java framework optimized for building cloud-native, containerized applications with fast startup times and low memory footprint, often used with Kubernetes.

name: Razor
description: Markup syntax used in ASP.NET Core for embedding server-side C# code within HTML to generate dynamic web page views.

name: React
description: JavaScript library for building user interfaces using a component-based architecture. Widely used for single-page applications and as the foundation for many other frontend frameworks.

name: React Native
description: Framework for building cross-platform mobile applications using JavaScript and React, rendering to native UI components on iOS and Android.

name: Recharts
description: Charting library for React built on top of D3, providing composable components for creating common chart types like line, bar, and pie charts.

name: Redux
description: Predictable state container for JavaScript applications, commonly used with React, that centralizes application state and enforces unidirectional data flow through actions and reducers.

name: Remix
description: Full-stack web framework built on React that focuses on server-side rendering, nested routing, and data loading, aiming to improve performance and user experience for web applications.

name: Retrofit
description: Type-safe HTTP client library for Java and Android that turns REST API endpoints into simple Java interface method calls.

name: Ruby on Rails
description: Web application framework written in Ruby that follows the MVC pattern and convention-over-configuration principles to speed up building database-backed web apps.

name: RxJS
description: Library for reactive programming in JavaScript using observables, enabling composition of asynchronous and event-based programs through operators like map, filter, and merge.

name: RxSwift
description: Reactive programming library for Swift that lets developers compose asynchronous and event-based code using observable sequences, based on the ReactiveX model.

name: Socket.IO
description: JavaScript library that enables real-time, bidirectional communication between web clients and servers, built on top of WebSockets with fallback support.

name: Spring Boot
description: Java framework that simplifies building standalone, production-ready Spring applications by providing auto-configuration and embedded servers, reducing boilerplate setup.

name: Spring Data
description: Part of the Spring ecosystem that simplifies data access, offering consistent, repository-based abstractions for working with relational and NoSQL databases.

name: Spring MVC
description: Web framework within Spring for building server-side Java web applications and REST APIs using the model-view-controller pattern.

name: Spring WebFlux
description: Reactive web framework within Spring for building non-blocking, asynchronous web applications and APIs on top of reactive streams.

name: Swift Charts
description: Apple framework for building data visualizations and charts declaratively within SwiftUI applications.

name: SwiftUI
description: Apple's declarative framework for building user interfaces across iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS using Swift.

name: Tailwind CSS
description: Utility-first CSS framework that provides low-level classes for styling elements directly in markup, allowing developers to build custom designs without writing separate CSS files.

name: Telerik
description: Suite of UI component libraries and developer tools from Progress Software for building web, desktop, and mobile applications across platforms like .NET, React, and Angular.

name: Three.js
description: JavaScript library that simplifies creating and rendering 3D graphics in web browsers using WebGL, commonly used for visualizations, games, and interactive experiences.

name: TinyMCE
description: Web-based rich text editor that can be embedded into applications to provide WYSIWYG content editing capabilities, similar to a word processor, within a browser.

name: UIKit
description: Apple's framework for building user interfaces on iOS and related platforms using an imperative, object-oriented approach, predating SwiftUI.

name: Unity Container
description: Lightweight dependency injection container for .NET applications that helps manage object creation and lifetime to support loosely coupled designs.

name: Universal Windows Platform
description: Microsoft platform for developing applications that run across multiple Windows device types, including PCs, tablets, and Xbox, using a common API set.

name: Vite
description: Frontend build tool and development server that provides fast hot module replacement and optimized bundling, commonly used with frameworks like Vue and React.

name: Vue.js
description: Progressive JavaScript framework for building user interfaces and single-page applications, known for its approachable learning curve and component-based architecture.

name: Windows Communication Foundation (WCF)
description: .NET framework for building service-oriented applications, enabling communication between distributed systems using configurable protocols and bindings.

name: Windows Forms
description: UI framework in .NET for building desktop applications on Windows using a drag-and-drop designer and event-driven programming model.

name: Windows Presentation Foundation
description: UI framework in .NET for building desktop applications on Windows, using XAML for declarative interface design and supporting rich graphics, data binding, and styling.

name: WordPress
description: Open-source content management system used to build and manage websites and blogs, extensible through plugins and themes.

name: Xamarin
description: Microsoft framework for building cross-platform mobile applications using C# and .NET, compiling to native code for iOS and Android.

name: Xamarin.Forms
description: UI toolkit built on top of Xamarin that lets developers share a single C# codebase for user interfaces across iOS, Android, and Windows.
